correctness.rationale: With length and time rescaled by L and L/v, write f_+-f_-=C-2x and (f_++f_-)/2=S+p(Cx-x^2). These solve the bulk equations. Exponential competition at each wall gives u S-(u/2+h)C=1 on the left and (B-u)[S+p(C-1)+C/2-1]+h(C-2)=1 on the right. Their determinant Q=Bh+(p+1)u(B-u) is positive throughout [0,B]. The expectation is finite including budget endpoints: one active wall has rate at least B/2, and from any state there is uniformly positive probability of reaching that wall and absorbing in bounded time (no bulk reversal during each traverse, and timely inward release if necessary at the other wall). The resulting geometric tail justifies the mean-time problem. Solving the system gives the stated C and S. For t=2u/B-1 the ensemble objective derivative is C'(u)[delta/2+(p+1)t/(1+eta t^2)], with C'(u)>0. The bracket is strictly increasing in t because eta<1, and its endpoint signs are strict since |delta|<=p+1<2(p+1)/(1+eta), even with deterministic initial direction. Thus the unique interior zero is the global minimum. Rationalizing the quadratic root yields the claimed radical and gives left preference iff delta<0. Strict spatial and directional monotonicity follow by inversion of the increasing scalar map, and the local derivative in delta is -B/[4(p+1)], yielding both stated response coefficients.
residual_risks: The conclusion is about unconditional absorption time with positive detachment and reversal rates and an interior start; it does not require an extension to singular rates or starts on a wall.

originality.rationale: The sticky-boundary process and the exact unbiased-start mean are established background. The distinct result is the global fixed-sum allocation theorem for arbitrary initial direction distributions, with an explicit criterion for bias to reverse the spatial preference and an orientation response independent of the detachment rate. A later catalogue theorem covers the unbiased-start optimization directly and is credited as exact overlap for that subcase; it does not state the biased-orientation result.
residual_risks: A bounded literature comparison cannot exclude an earlier biased-start optimization under another boundary vocabulary. The later indexed exact overlap does not establish the historical relationship between the two records.

value.rationale: A joint budget creates a genuine constrained decision about whether to use both walls or concentrate capture at one. The solution rules out either corner even for a strongly directed start, quantifies the split, and identifies precisely when initial motion overrides proximity. The global result and its orientation response are useful beyond evaluation of a known unbiased mean at a chosen allocation.
residual_risks: This is an exact result for the specified one-dimensional conserved-rate model, not a general rule about capture probabilities under other mechanisms or time horizons.
